title: French web host LWS says its WHOIS server was accessed without authorisation
date_note: Clubic's page, published 27 November, gives no earlier date for LWS's customer email; the page says LWS detected the access on 16 November.
geo_basis: country: Clubic names LWS as a French host and gives no city
summary: According to Clubic, which relays LWS's email to customers, LWS detected unauthorised access to the server of its WHOIS service on 16 November and notified the CNIL. LWS says names, postal addresses, phone numbers, contact emails, domain names and customer account numbers may have been copied, including data hidden in the public WHOIS listing. It says no banking data was involved and passwords and services were not affected.
plain: LWS, a French web host, told customers that someone got into the server behind its domain-owner directory and may have copied contact details. LWS says passwords and bank data were not involved.
exec: LWS says contact details and domain names of its customers may have been copied, which could be used for convincing scam messages about domains.
action: LWS advises changing your password if you sent support a message containing one, being wary of unusual requests to pay, renew or transfer a domain, and checking them in your LWS customer area before paying.

validation.note: Only Clubic was read; it relays LWS's customer email. No LWS page was read and Clubic gives no count of people affected.
